messages:
maria: Heads up — p99 tail latency jumped from ~480ms to 3.2s on runtime-pool-eu-west1 between 09:12-09:22 UTC. Seen across 3 hosts. KV cache eviction rate spiked at the same time. Profiling shows frequent kernel swaps (matmul-fp16-opt <-> matmul-int8-fallback) during the same windows.
noah: link to grafana: https://grafana.company/runtime/pool/eu-west1?range=10m :eyes:
lee: Any tenant(s) correlated? noisy neighbor?
maria: Primary offender looks like tenant=search-synthesis-prod. Query shows median prompt tokens up from ~1.2k -> ~9.6k for ~1500 requests in that window. Also ~120 requests show repeated tool-calls (looping tool invocation) which keeps producing new tokens and re-entering the runtime, causing long lived KV entries and eviction churn.
anya: Can we reproduce locally? If kernel is swapping we might be hitting heuristics that pick int8 for long sequences then fall back. Could be quant-fallback on certain layers under high seq length.
lee: Quick mitigation options: 1) throttle per-request tool-call loop (guard rails), 2) temporarily pin kernel variant for this tenant to fp16, 3) move tenant to a dedicated (isolated) queue. Which one do we do now?
maria: I pushed a quick read-only query to confirm: logs show repeated tool-call idempotency failures -> code path keeps reissuing tool call. So this is a request anomaly (tool loop) + long prompts. Agreed we should isolate tenant first.
noah: I'll try a soft-route to dedicated pool (no config change, just routing) for search-synthesis-prod. Command:```bash
# route tenant to dedicated pool eu-west1-dedicated-1
curl -s -X POST "https://control-plane/api/v1/routing/override" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CTL_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"tenant":"search-synthesis-prod","target":"eu-west1-dedicated-1","ttl_s":3600}'
```
maria: Doing that now. Also increasing scheduler weight for seq-length so batching doesn't coalesce long tails with short requests. Patch: set scheduler.config.length_penalty=0.75 -> apply to pool.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: routing override accepted (id=rv-1382).
perf-bot: perf-bot: snapshot collected -> p50: 130ms, p95: 240ms, p99: 3.2s (pre-mitigation). KV evictions/sec peaked at 14k -> baseline 900.
noah: After routing override p99 dropped to ~620ms within 90s. KV evictions fell back to ~1.1k. Looks promising.
anya: Good. For root cause: we should instrument kernel selector to log decision reasons (why int8 chosen then fallback). Also add a guard in scheduler: don't batch huge sequences with small ones; use sequence bucketing by length.
lee: Action items: - maria/anya to add kernel-selector debug logs + a short profile capturing per-request kernel decisions (1h capture) - noah to convert routing override into a short-lived policy and add a 'noisy-tenant' annotation - infra to add a watchdog that marks tenants doing >3 tool calls per request in 5m and rate-limits them.
maria: Quick note: I see some streaming backpressure on client connections for these long requests (frontend logs show stalled streams). That explains client-side retries and extra tool-call churn. We'll also purge stuck KV entries older than 600s on that pool.
noah: Purge command run. Monitoring shows eviction rate trending down.
anya: For follow-up: reproduce with a fuzzed request containing nested tool loops and ~10k tokens, run the kernel selection profiler on the reproduce env, and check quant-fallback thresholds. I'll own the reproducer and profiler capture.
lee: Thanks — leave this thread open. If p99 remains <700ms for 30m we can close. Also add postmortem notes if we need longer term fixes. :thumbsup:
